# ethereum-optimism/infra Daily Update (Jul 30, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's focus was on security updates, with several dependency bumps to address vulnerabilities. A new pull request was opened to fix memory leaks in the op-ufm component. Discussions continued on critical issues, including a supernode derivation fork and a flaky sequencer failover test.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Dependency Security Updates
Several security-related dependency updates were implemented to enhance the overall security posture of the `replica-healthcheck` component. These updates include bumping `tmp` to v0.2.7, `postcss` to v8.5.18, and `linkify-it` to v5.0.2. ([#684](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/684), [#683](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/683), [#682](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/682))

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- A new pull request, [#685](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/685), was opened to address memory leaks in the provider transaction pool and RPC clients within the `op-ufm` component.

## CLOSED ISSUES
- None

## NEW ISSUES
- A critical issue, [#22138](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/22138), was opened regarding the `op-supernode` derivation silently forking after an invalidation replacement, leading to `logsDB` recovery failures.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### Supernode Derivation Fork and LogsDB Recovery Failure
Discussion on [#22138](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/22138) revealed that the issue is more widespread than initially thought, affecting the entire devnet's cross-safe head, not just a single supernode's `logsDB`. The `optimism_syncStatus` shows that `safe_l2` is significantly stale across all CL nodes, indicating a frozen cross-safe head. The root cause was revised: the supernode silently forked its derivation pipeline at block 259687, two blocks after an invalidation replacement, and continued to verify against this private fork. This led to a deadlock where the `logsDB` frontier was pinned at a `lastValidParentBlock` that was later re-derived as part of a different chain. The discussion highlighted a detection gap, as existing alerts did not flag the cross-safe lag. A fix would either prevent the derivation rebuild from affecting `lastValidParentBlock` or allow `logsDB` to rewind further on a `super authority safe head non-canonical` signal.

### Kona SP1 Proposer Sync Games Decomposition
The discussion on [#22019](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/22019) focused on refactoring the `sync_games` function in the `kona-sp1-proposer` to improve maintainability and consolidate state management. A key point raised was to unify the `last_created_game_l2_sequence_number`, `last_created_game_address`, and `in_flight_creation` fields into a single lifecycle value, representing the state of the latest game creation. This consolidation aims to streamline the logic for tracking game creation status, from unconfirmed to confirmed, until it's visible in the cache.

### Flaky Test: TestSequencerFailover_ConductorRPC
Investigation into the flaky `TestSequencerFailover_ConductorRPC` test in [#22094](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/22094) identified two main defects. The dominant failure signature, a 30-second deadline timeout, was traced to `op-conductor`. It was found that if a sequencer falls two or more blocks behind consensus, the conductor can wedge indefinitely without transferring leadership. A fix is proposed to allow the FSM to replay missing payloads, wait for adoption, and escalate to a leader transfer if necessary. The second defect, a 20-minute hang, was due to `RaftConsensus.Shutdown` blocking indefinitely, causing the entire test teardown to stall. A fix for this involves bounding the `raft.Shutdown().Error()` call. A draft PR has been created to address both issues.
